source_semantics.control: AI Center exposes Refresh state only after an approval has been submitted in the current source session.
source_semantics.authoritative_read: RefreshApprovalStatus calls ApprovalService.GetById(_ownerUserId, _lastApprovalId) and replaces only the displayed approval status.
source_semantics.side_effects: The source refresh performs no approval mutation, persistence write, WordPress operation, AI-provider call, queue action, or navigation.

laravel_adaptation.frontend: resources/js/ai-center-approval-status-control.tsx exposes the exact Refresh state control only after a real persisted current-user approval is returned and marks only that button with AIMW-AI-168B406674.
laravel_adaptation.read_authority: GET /api/tenants/{tenant}/ai-center/approval-status is authenticated, tenant-context-bound, authorized by ai.use, tenant-scoped through Approval's DomainModel scope, and additionally restricted to actor_user_id = the authenticated user.
laravel_adaptation.independent_rehydration: Because the separate Submit operation is outside this worker's ownership, Laravel intentionally ADAPTS the source session-only _lastApprovalId by rehydrating the latest persisted approval owned by the authenticated user in the active tenant.
laravel_adaptation.refresh_behavior: Clicking Refresh state repeats the same GET-only authoritative read and reconciles the displayed status from the server; it sends no request body and invokes no mutation contract.
laravel_adaptation.guard: Missing ai.use, missing owned approval, read failure, or tenant mismatch does not fabricate a refresh surface.

tenant_isolation.same_tenant_user_boundary: Focused acceptance creates two users in one tenant and proves the authenticated user never receives the other user's newer approval.
tenant_isolation.cross_tenant_boundary: Focused acceptance proves a user authenticated only in Alpha receives 404 when requesting Beta's tenant route.
tenant_isolation.id_surface: The adaptation accepts no caller-supplied approval ID, so the current-user ownership boundary cannot be bypassed by guessing an approval identifier.
